proposed.explanation:
Profit attributable to CIB's (COMI) own shareholders was EGP 82,238,852,000 for the year ended 31 Dec 2025, up from EGP 55,196,394,000 in 2024 – an increase of EGP 27,042,458,000, or roughly 49 %. This was driven largely by net interest income, which rose from EGP 91,064,222,000 to EGP 107,699,631,000 (+18.3 %). The small gap between total net profit (EGP 82,258,815,000) and the amount attributable to the bank's shareholders (EGP 82,238,852,000) indicates that non-controlling interests are negligible.

For your 7-year bank-income goal, this ~49 % profit growth is encouraging and supports keeping your existing 250-share position. However, I am not recommending a buy: your COMI holding (250 × 128 = EGP 32,000) already represents about 61.5 % of your total portfolio (EGP 52,000 including cash), which exceeds the 50 % single-company concentration limit. Adding more shares would deepen that concentration further. If you wish to add to the position in the future, you would first need to diversify into other holdings.

Risks and uncertainty: the figures are for a single fiscal year; a 49 % jump can reflect one-off items, a low base in 2024, or a favourable interest-rate environment that may not persist. Bank earnings are sensitive to credit cycles, regulatory changes, and macroeconomic conditions in Egypt. This is guidance, not a guarantee of future returns. I would monitor the next two or three annual reports to confirm the growth is sustainable before considering any further allocation.
